title: SB 253 and SB 261: What California's Climate Disclosure Laws Mean for Fashion Brands
summary: SB 253 and SB 261 explained for fashion brands: who is in scope, how to file the first report by November 10, 2026, and what changes in 2027.
body_markdown:
> Status: ✅ SB 253: Scope 1 & 2 due November 10, 2026; Scope 3 from 2027. SB 261 is paused.


For apparel and footwear brands doing business in California, new climate disclosure requirements are taking effect under SB 253 (the Climate Corporate Data Accountability Act) and SB 261 (the Climate-Related Financial Risk Act). Together, these laws set state-level rules for how large brands must report greenhouse gas emissions and climate-related financial risks.


The first SB 253 deadline for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions is November 10, 2026. Large apparel and footwear companies such as Columbia Sportswear, Under Armour and Crocs are among those[CARB expects to report](https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/our-work/programs/corporate-ghg-reporting/resources#:~:text=Preliminary%20List%20of%20Reporting/Covered%20Entities%20(posted%209/24/2025)) .


Scope 3 reporting will begin in 2027. This means fashion brands should start preparing Scope 3 data now: establish processes to collect supplier data and document calculations and assumptions using the GHG Protocol as a foundation.


Below, see who is in scope, what to send for the first report, and how to prepare for 2027.


Looking for a Carbon Accounting solution? Find our complete, hands-on guide to[Carbon Accounting and the GHG Protocol for apparel and footwear](https://www.carbonfact.com/blog/knowledge/carbon-accounting-guide) brands here.


#### TL;DR


- **SB 253** applies to US-registered companies (including US subsidiaries of foreign groups) with over $1 billion in annual revenue doing business in California and requires disclosure of greenhouse gas emissions. The first Scope 1 and Scope 2 report is due November 10, 2026. Scope 3 is expected from 2027.


- **SB 261** applies to companies with over $500 million in revenue and requires disclosure of climate-related financial risks. CARB is not enforcing SB 261 while a court case is ongoing; reporting is voluntary.


- Together, these laws are known as California's Climate Accountability Package.


## What Is SB 253 and What Must Fashion Brands Report?


SB 253 (the Climate Corporate Data Accountability Act) introduces mandatory[greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions](https://www.carbonfact.com/blog/knowledge/carbon-accounting-guide) reporting for large companies doing business in California. For apparel and footwear brands, this marks the start of regulated emissions disclosure at the state level.


SB 253 requires in-scope brands to measure and disclose their emissions in line with the GHG Protocol:


-


Scope 1 emissions:


direct emissions from sources the brand owns or controls, from 2026.


-


Scope 2 emissions:


indirect emissions from purchased energy, from 2026.


-


Scope 3 emissions:


value-chain emissions, from 2027.


For fashion brands with complex global supply chains, Scope 3 will be particularly significant. It requires data beyond direct operations, including raw material sourcing, supplier manufacturing, and logistics.


## Which Apparel and Footwear Brands Are Affected by SB 253?


A fashion brand is in scope of SB 253 if all three of the following conditions are met:


1.


It is a U.S. company (or a U.S. subsidiary):


The brand has a legal company registered in the United States. This includes U.S. subsidiaries of international fashion groups.


2.


It exceeds $1 billion in annual revenue:


The company or subsidiary had more than $1 billion in revenue in each of its last two fiscal years (CARB uses the lower of the two). Revenue is counted for each company separately, not for the group as a whole.


3.


It does business in California:


**** A company is considered to be doing business in California if at least one of the following applies:


1.


It is registered in California, or its headquarters is in California.


2.


Its California sales are above the threshold ($757,070 for 2025, or 25% of total sales, whichever is lower).


This means SB 253 does not apply to all fashion brands. It targets large companies that meet specific revenue and California business thresholds.


CARB’s preliminary list of potentially covered entities[includes fashion brands](https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/our-work/programs/corporate-ghg-reporting/resources#:~:text=Preliminary%20List%20of%20Reporting/Covered%20Entities%20(posted%209/24/2025)) such as Nike, Inc., Skechers U.S.A., Inc., PVH Corp., Tapestry, The Gap, Inc. and Deckers Outdoor Corporation


## What Is the SB 253 Timeline?


The first deadline is November 10, 2026


, for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions. Its rules for the first report are now final. Requirements increase in 2027. Let’s break it down:


### What Do Fashion Brands Need to Report in 2026?


For apparel and footwear brands, 2026 is the first reporting year under SB 253 and is designed as a transition period.


Brands report Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions for the prior fiscal year, using data they already had or were collecting on December 5, 2024. Brands without data send a statement instead. Assurance is not required to file.


### What Changes in 2027?


2027 is the first year that Scope 3 emissions would be reported under SB 253. Scope 3 covers emissions in the value chain, outside a brand’s own operations. For apparel and footwear brands, Scope 3 is usually most of the footprint, mainly from materials and manufacturing.


For 2027, CARB proposes:


-


Scope 3 reporting in five categories:


purchased goods and services (Category 1), fuel- and energy-related activities (3), waste (5), business travel (6) and employee commuting (7).


-


Limited assurance


on Scope 1 and Scope 2, checked by an independent third party.


-


A yearly deadline of November 10.


Category 1 needs material and production data from suppliers, so brands should start collecting it now. To avoid repeating the same manual work every year, we recommend using an emissions management tool.

## How Should Fashion Brands Prepare Their First SB 253 Submission?


The first report is due November 10, 2026. It covers Scope 1 and Scope 2 only.[CARB's reporting guidance](https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/2026-09/2026_SB253_Reporting_Guidance.pdf) makes this first year lighter than later years. Here are the steps for your first submission:


### 1. Confirm the Brand Is in-Scope


Check each U.S. legal entity against the three conditions above. Each company is responsible for its own assessment. If several group entities are in scope, the parent can file one consolidated report.


### 2. Find the Right Fiscal Year


-


Fiscal year ends on or before February 1


(e.g., January 31, 2026): report the fiscal year that ended in 2026.


-


Fiscal year ends after February 1


(e.g., December 31): report the fiscal year that ended in 2025. Brands may report a more recent year if the data is ready.


### 3. Define the Reporting Boundary and Collect Data


Decide which operations and facilities the report includes. The GHG Protocol offers three approaches: operational control, financial control, or equity share. The law covers Scope 1 and 2 emissions “regardless of location”, so the boundary includes operations worldwide, not just in California.


For this first report, brands may use data they already had or were collecting on December 5, 2024. They don’t have to collect new data just for this report.


### 4. Choose and Disclose Emission Factors


No specific dataset is required for Scope 2. Brands can use the US EPA’s eGRID 2023, the eGRID 2024 dataset from the Cornerstone Sustainability Data Initiative, or another credible source. CARB encourages brands to name the factors and sources used.


### 5. Document Methods and Assumptions


Explain any estimates and proxies used to fill data gaps. CARB encourages brands to describe their methodology, data sources and assumptions. This also prepares the brand for assurance, expected from 2027.


### 6. Choose What to Submit


CARB accepts four formats for 2026:


- An existing annual or sustainability report that includes Scope 1 and 2 emissions.


- Scope 1 and 2 data already reported to another program or voluntary initiative, such as CDP.


- CARB's draft Scope 1 and 2 reporting template (Excel, published October 10, 2025). Its use is voluntary.


-


A statement of non-reporting , if the brand had no Scope 1 and 2 data and was not collecting and not planning to collect any on December 5, 2024. These statements will be made public.


### 7. Assurance Is Not Needed to File in 2026


Assurance means an independent third party checks the reported emissions. For this first year, CARB accepts reports without assurance. From 2027, CARB proposes to require limited assurance on Scope 1 and Scope 2.


### 8. Submit by November 10, 2026


Use CARB's voluntary intake platform on the[Climate Disclosure webpage](https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/our-work/programs/california-corporate-greenhouse-gas-ghg-reporting-and-climate-related-financial) , or email climatedisclosure@arb.ca.gov. The platform also collects billing contacts: CARB sends fee notices by December 10, and fees must be paid within 60 days.

## What Are the Penalties Under SB 253?


-


Maximum penalty:


Apparel and footwear brands that fail to file required reports or comply with SB 253 may face penalties of up to $500,000 per reporting year.


-


Enforcement body:


**** The California Air Resources Board (CARB) oversees compliance.


-


Factors considered:


CARB considers the brand’s past and present compliance, and whether and when it took good-faith steps to comply.


-


Scope 3 protection:


Brands are not penalized for Scope 3 misstatements made with a reasonable basis and disclosed in good faith. Until 2030, Scope 3 penalties apply only to failing to file. This protection does not apply to Scope 1 or Scope 2 emissions.


## What Does SB 261 Mean for Fashion Brands?


SB 261 (the Climate-Related Financial Risk Act) requires large brands to assess and disclose how climate change could impact their financial performance and operations. Unlike SB 253, SB 261 does not focus on emissions data, but on climate-related risks and how companies manage them.


## Which Apparel and Footwear Brands Are Affected by SB 261?


SB 261 applies to US-registered companies, including US subsidiaries of foreign groups, with over $500 million in total annual revenue that do business in California.


-


Revenue counts sales worldwide


, not just in California.


-


It’s calculated per company


, not for the whole group.


-


CARB uses the lower of the last two fiscal years.


-


“Doing business in California”


follows the same definition as SB 253.


## What Is the Status of SB 261?


SB 261 was adopted in 2023 with an initial reporting deadline in January 2026; however, the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals ordered a pause while a legal challenge is heard. CARB has confirmed it will not enforce SB 261 for now, and that reporting is voluntary.[More than 120 companies have filed reports voluntarily](https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/news/carb-approves-climate-transparency-regulation-entities-doing-business-california) , and a new reporting timeline will be announced once enforcement resumes.


## What Would Fashion Companies Need to Report Under SB 261?


SB 261 requires companies to publish a climate-related financial risk report every two years and make it publicly available.


The report should:


- Identify and assess the company’s exposure to climate-related financial risks.
- Describe the measures taken to mitigate and adapt to those risks.


*(Both of these bear similarity to the*[Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive](https://www.carbonfact.com/blog/csrd-textile) *’s (CSRD) double materiality assessment.)*


The reported risks fall into two main categories: physical and transition.


-


Physical risks


stem from the direct impacts of climate change, such as extreme weather events, rising sea levels, or wildfires. These risks can disrupt supply chains, damage manufacturing facilities, and increase raw material costs.


-


Transition risks


, on the other hand, arise from shifts toward a low-carbon economy. These include changes in government regulations, technological advancements, and evolving consumer preferences.


Reports should be aligned with the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) framework or equivalent standards such as ISSB. While TCFD was formally disbanded in 2023, its recommendations were incorporated into the ISSB standards. As a result, fashion brands already reporting under ISSB or International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) are largely aligned with SB 261 requirements.


The four key elements of the TCFD framework are:


-


Governance


– how an organization will structure its business operations in response to climate-related risks.


-


Strategy


**** – how climate-related risks will impact a company’s strategy, business operations, and financial planning.


-


Risk management


– how an organization will identify, assess, and manage climate-related risks.


-


Metrics and targets


– how an organization will measure climate-related risks and opportunities.


Companies are allowed to publish parent-level reports as well as financial risk disclosures that have already been prepared in accordance with other reporting requirements like CSRD.

### SB 253 FAQ


##### What is SB 253?


SB 253, the Climate Corporate Data Accountability Act, is a California law that requires large U.S. companies doing business in California to report their greenhouse gas emissions to CARB every year: Scope 1 and 2 from 2026, and Scope 3 from 2027.


##### Does SB 253 apply to non-U.S. fashion brands?


Only through their U.S. entities. A U.S. subsidiary with over $1 billion in revenue that does business in California is in scope.


##### When is the SB 253 reporting deadline?


The first Scope 1 and Scope 2 report is due November 10, 2026. CARB proposes November 10 as the yearly deadline from 2027.


##### Does SB 253 apply to non-U.S. fashion brands?


##### What if a brand has no Scope 1 and 2 data for 2026?


If it was not collecting data on December 5, 2024, it can send CARB a statement of non-reporting on company letterhead instead of a report.


##### Is assurance required for the first SB 253 report?


No. CARB will accept 2026 reports with or without assurance. Limited assurance is expected to apply from 2027.


##### Where do brands submit their SB 253 report?


Through CARB's optional intake platform on its Climate Disclosure webpage, or by email to climatedisclosure@arb.ca.gov.
